title: Roumanian couching
subtitle: A self-couching stitch that lays and ties thread in one movement
excerpt: Roumanian couching lays a long thread across a shape and ties it down with a slanted stitch in the same continuous thread movement. No separate couching thread is needed. The result is an angled filling stitch with a distinctive slanted tie pattern across the shape.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), couching and laid work chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), Roumanian stitch entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stitch technique where the same thread that crosses the shape is brought back to tie itself down, without a separate couching thread.

heroPrompt: Roumanian couching filling a large leaf in soft sage green stranded cotton on cream linen, showing the diagonal slanted ties across the parallel laid threads, natural light.

content.text: fill: the thread is carried across the shape, then the needle re-enters the fabric a short way from the exit point and comes up on the far side of the crossing thread. A short slanted tie stitch holds the laid thread down.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton 3 to 4 strands, or crewel wool

content.text: Bring the thread up at the left edge of the shape. Carry it across to the right edge and insert the needle just inside the right edge.
Bring the needle up a short distance inside the right edge, just below the crossing thread.
Take a short slanted stitch over the crossing thread toward the centre of the shape to tie it down.
Carry the thread across again for the next row, spacing it just below the previous tie stitch.

items.fix: Mark parallel guide lines across the shape before starting. Equal spacing gives a regular pattern.

items.symptom: The tie stitches are too long and dominate the design
items.cause: The tie stitch is too far from the edge.
items.fix: The tie stitch should be short, about 3 to 4 mm, placed in the centre of the shape. Only the tie slant should show; the laid thread underneath should dominate.

content.text: Roumanian couching fills large shapes well in crewelwork and Jacobean embroidery. The self-couching idea also appears in Jacobean laid work and trellis couching.
